title: Travel and timetables
cando: read a timetable, book a journey and deal with a delay

about.text: In this lesson you plan a trip and book a seat and a room. You read a timetable, a platform notice and a weather warning. Then you deal with a cancelled train.
goals: Ask about times: When does it leave? Is there a later one?
Book a ticket and a room: I'd like to book…
Choose a future form: it leaves, I'm flying, I'm going to, I'll.
Read a timetable, a platform notice and a weather warning.
Deal with a cancellation, and write a message about a delay.

chapters.title: The evening before a trip
chapters.text:
In this lesson you travel, and you deal with problems on the way.
First, you listen to Priya. It is the evening before a work trip abroad.
Her flight leaves tomorrow morning. She phones a coach company to book a seat to the airport.
She asks: When does the first coach leave? It is too early, so she asks: Is there a later one?
Listen carefully for the times. Fifteen and fifty sound different: fif-TEEN, FIF-ty.

chapters.title: Four ways to talk about the future
chapters.text:
In English, there are four ways to talk about the future.
One: a time on a timetable. Use the present simple. The coach leaves at 6:10.
Two: an arrangement, with a ticket or with a person. I'm flying to Lisbon tomorrow.
Three: a plan from before. I'm going to pack tonight.
Four: a decision you make as you speak, or a guess. I'll take the 6:10. You'll have time.
Choose the right one, and people understand how fixed your plan is.

chapters.title: A timetable, a notice and a warning
chapters.text:
Next, you read three short documents from a station.
The timetable says when the trains leave and arrive. Some run daily. One runs on Fridays and Saturdays only. Look at the days, not only the times.
The platform notice says which trains are late or cancelled today.
The weather warning says what the storm will do. Read it before you travel.
Then you write a message about a delay. Say what happened, and give your new time.

chapters.title: Planning a trip
chapters.text:
In the task, you plan a trip for work. First, you read the timetable and choose a train.
Then you book a ticket at the station, and a room at a hostel.
But then there is a problem. Your train is cancelled.
Ask the clerk: Is there a later one? Then call the hostel and give your new arrival time.

chapters.title: The book
chapters.text:
Last, you read a story or an article about a journey.
Read it once for the story. Then read it again and answer the questions.

warmup.prompt: You are going on a trip tomorrow. When do you pack?
choices: on the morning of the trip
warmup.note: There is no wrong answer. Many people pack the night before. Then the morning is calm, and they don't forget their passport.

conversation.title: Booking the airport coach
conversation.setting: It is Sunday evening. Priya is flying abroad tomorrow for a fortnight of training. She phones Westway Coaches. A coach is a big bus for long journeys.
lines: Westway Coaches, good evening. How can I help?
Hello. I'm flying to Lisbon tomorrow, and I'd like to book a seat to the airport.
Of course. What time does your flight leave?
At half past nine. When does the first coach leave?
The first one leaves at 5:15. It arrives at the airport at 6:30.
That's very early. Is there a later one?
Yes, there's a direct coach at 6:10. It gets to the airport at 7:05.
Is that OK for a flight at half past nine?
Yes. You have to check in before 8:50, so you'll have time.
Fine. How much luggage have you got?
Just one big suitcase. I'm going to pack it tonight.
That's no problem. It's £18. You'll get your booking number by text in a minute.
Thank you. The 6:10, direct to the airport. Perfect!

questions.q: Why doesn't Priya want the first coach?
questions.why: Priya says: That's very early. Is there a later one?

questions.q: What time does the 6:10 coach get to the airport?
questions.why: The clerk says: It gets to the airport at 7:05.

questions.q: What is Priya going to do tonight?
questions.why: Priya says: I'm going to pack it tonight.

phrases.text: I'd like to book a seat, please.
When does the first coach leave?
phrases.use: Asking about a time on the timetable.
Asking for a train or a coach after that time.

phrases.text: Is that OK for a flight at half past nine?
How much luggage have you got?
phrases.use: A question you often hear when you book.
Saying a plan that is fixed, with a ticket.

items.meaning: A seat, a room or a table that you ask for before you go.
items.example: I made a booking for two nights at the hotel.

items.meaning: When you get to a place. Also: the time when a train or a plane gets there.
items.example: What's the arrival time of your flight?

items.meaning: A short journey from an airport or a station to your hotel.
items.example: The hotel has a free transfer from the airport.

items.meaning: The bags and suitcases that you take on a trip. Say luggage, not luggages.
items.example: How much luggage have you got?

items.meaning: In another country, or to another country.
items.example: I'm going abroad for work next month.

items.meaning: A journey on a plane.
items.example: My flight leaves at 9:30.

items.meaning: A paper or a stamp in your passport. It says you can go into a country.
items.example: Do I need a visa for Canada?

items.meaning: Two weeks. People in the UK use this word a lot.
items.example: I'm going on holiday for a fortnight.

items.meaning: To show your ticket and give your bags at the airport. Also: to arrive at a hotel and get your key.
items.example: You have to check in two hours before the flight.

items.meaning: To put your clothes and things in a bag for a trip.
items.example: I always pack the night before I travel.

items.meaning: To need to pay money to a person, for example money they paid for you.
items.example: You paid for my ticket, so I owe you £20.

items.meaning: Going from one place to another with no stops and no changes.
items.example: Is there a direct train, or do I have to change?

items.meaning: A cheap place to stay. You often share a room with other people.
items.example: We stayed in a hostel near the station.

items.meaning: The card, or the page on your phone, that lets you get on the plane.
items.example: Have your boarding pass ready at the gate.

sound.title: fifteen or fifty?
sound.explain: Listen to these numbers. In fifteen, the strong part is at the end: fif-TEEN. In fifty, it is at the start: FIF-ty. Times and prices depend on it. Listen, then say each group.
lines: The first coach leaves at five fifteen.
It's gate fifty, not gate fifteen.

sayIt.instructions: Say Priya's lines. Record yourself, then listen back. Are your times clear?
lines: Hello. I'm flying to Lisbon tomorrow, and I'd like to book a seat to the airport.
At half past nine. When does the first coach leave?
That's very early. Is there a later one?
Just one big suitcase. I'm going to pack it tonight.

spot.instructions: Look at these sentences from the conversation. They are all about the future, but they use four different forms.
examples: I'm going to pack it tonight.
spot.question: Which one is a time on a timetable? Which one is fixed with a ticket? Which one is a plan from before? Which one is a decision Priya makes as she speaks?
spot.answer: Leaves at 5:15 is a timetable time, so it uses the present simple. I'm flying is an arrangement: Priya has a ticket. I'm going to pack is her plan from before. I'll take the 6:10 is a decision she makes now, as she speaks.

rules.title: The train leaves at six: timetables
rule: A time on a timetable: use the present simple, even for tomorrow.
The train leaves at 6:20. The coach arrives at 7:05.
Ask with does: What time does the flight leave? When does the office open?
One train, one shop: add s. It leaves, it opens, it closes.
Use it for trains, buses, flights, shops and courses. Not for your own plans.
rules.mistake: Not: What time the train leaves? Say: What time does the train leave?

rules.title: Choosing a future form for a trip
rule: A timetable: The flight leaves at 9:30.
An arrangement, with a ticket or a person: I'm flying to Lisbon on Monday.
A plan from before: I'm going to pack tonight.
A decision now, as you speak: There's no bus. I'll take a taxi.
A guess about the future: It'll be cold there. You'll have time.
rules.mistake: Not: I pack tonight (for your plan). Say: I'm going to pack tonight.

practice.why: A timetable time: the present simple, with s.
A timetable question: What time does it arrive?
No, with it: doesn't + the plain verb.

practice.q: I ___ my sister this weekend. I've got the tickets.
practice.why: An arrangement with a ticket: am + -ing.

practice.q: There's no coach after ten. — OK, I ___ take a taxi, then.
practice.why: A decision you make as you speak: I'll, or I will.

practice.q: Tonight I'm going to ___ my suitcase.
practice.why: going to + the plain verb: going to pack.

practice.q: The forecast says it ___ be icy tomorrow.
practice.why: A guess about the future: it will be.

practice.q: Are you free on Friday? — No, I ___ to Paris. My flight is at seven.
practice.why: An arrangement: I am flying. Do not forget am.

practice.q: The 6:10 is too early for me. Is there a ___ one?
practice.why: Is there a later one? asks for a coach after that time.
An arrangement: What time are you leaving? are + -ing.

yourTurn.prompt: You are going on a trip next week. Write four sentences about it. Use the four forms: a timetable, an arrangement, going to and I'll.
yourTurn.model: My train leaves at 7:40 on Monday. I'm staying with my cousin in Manchester for three nights. I'm going to pack on Sunday evening. It's a long journey, so I'll take a good book.

text.title: A timetable, a notice and a warning
text.type: Timetable, platform notice and weather warning
text.body:
PRACTICE DOCUMENTS: this railway and this forecast are not real.

NORTHLINE RAIL · TIMETABLE
Hillford to Westhaven, from 6 April

Leaves 06:20 · Arrives 08:05 · Daily
Leaves 09:40 · Arrives 11:25 · Daily
Leaves 14:10 · Arrives 15:55 · Monday to Saturday
Leaves 18:05 · Arrives 19:50 · Daily
Leaves 21:30 · Arrives 23:15 · Friday and Saturday only
All trains are direct. You can use weekly tickets on every train.

- - - - - - - -

PLATFORM 3 · NOTICE FOR PASSENGERS
Friday 10 April
Because of the storm, the 18:05 to Westhaven is cancelled.
Passengers for the 18:05 can take the 21:30 at no extra cost.
The 14:10 is running 40 minutes late.
We are sorry for the cancellation. Staff at the desk can change your booking.

- - - - - - - -

WEATHER WARNING · FRIDAY 10 APRIL
The forecast for this evening: heavy rain and strong wind.
Thunder and lightning after 5 pm.
There may be floods near the river. Do not drive through deep water.
Fog on the hills tomorrow morning. Roads will be icy after midnight.
Only travel if you need to.

gist.q: What is the big problem on Friday?
gist.a: a storm, with heavy rain and strong wind
gist.why: The warning says: heavy rain and strong wind, with thunder and lightning.

gist.q: Which document tells you the usual times of the trains?
gist.why: The timetable shows when every train leaves and arrives.

detail.q: You have a ticket for the 18:05. What can you do?
detail.a: take the 21:30 at no extra cost
detail.why: The notice says you can take the 21:30 at no extra cost.

detail.q: What time does the 14:10 leave today?
detail.why: It is running 40 minutes late, and 14:10 + 40 minutes = 14:50.

detail.q: Can you take the 21:30 on a Tuesday?
detail.a: No. It runs on Fridays and Saturdays only.
detail.why: The timetable says: Friday and Saturday only.

detail.q: What does the forecast say about tomorrow morning?
detail.a: There will be fog on the hills.
wrong: It will be hot and sunny.
detail.why: The warning says: Fog on the hills tomorrow morning.

items.meaning: Very bad weather, with strong wind and heavy rain.
items.example: The storm stopped all the trains to the coast.

items.meaning: When a plan, a train or a flight is stopped, and it does not happen.
items.example: There are two cancellations on the board this morning.

items.meaning: Happening every day.
items.example: There's a daily train to the airport at six.

items.meaning: Happening once a week. Also: for one week.
items.example: I buy a weekly ticket for the bus.

items.meaning: What the weather will probably be like. You see it on TV or on your phone.
items.example: The forecast says it will rain all weekend.

items.meaning: A lot of water on land that is usually dry.
items.example: After the storm, there was a flood in the town centre.

items.meaning: Thick cloud near the ground. It is hard to see through it.
items.example: Our flight was late because of fog.

items.meaning: The loud noise in the sky during a storm.
items.example: The thunder woke me up at three in the morning.

items.meaning: The bright light in the sky during a storm.
items.example: Don't stand under a tree when there is lightning.

items.meaning: Covered with ice. It is very cold, and people can fall.
items.example: Drive slowly. The roads are icy this morning.

model.title: A message about a delay
model.body:
Hi Lena,
Bad news, I'm afraid. Because of the storm, my 18:05 train is cancelled.
I'm taking the 21:30 instead. It arrives in Westhaven at 23:15.
So I'm going to miss dinner tonight. Sorry!
I'll see you at the training at nine tomorrow.
Omar

write.task: Your train or your flight is late or cancelled. Write a message to the person who is meeting you. Say what happened, give your new time, and say what you will do now.
write.starter: Hi …, bad news, I'm afraid. My …
checklist: I said what happened: delayed or cancelled, and why.
I gave my new time, like a timetable: It arrives at …
I used a future form: I'm taking…, I'm going to… or I'll…
I said sorry and wrote my name at the end.

card.title: A work trip to Westhaven
card.situation: Your company is sending you to a training day in Westhaven on Saturday morning. You travel on Friday after work and stay one night. Use the timetable in Section 3.
card.goal: Choose a train and book a ticket. Book a room for Friday night. Then your train is cancelled. Ask for a later one, and call the hostel again.

phrases: I'd like to book a seat on the 18:05, please.
I'd like to book a room for Friday night.
My train is cancelled, so I'm arriving at 23:15.
I'll be there at about eight.
prepare.notes: Look at the timetable and choose a train. Write down the times. Then plan what you will say if your train is cancelled.

doIt.liveClass: In the live class, your teacher is the ticket clerk, then the hostel receptionist. Book your ticket and your room. Then your teacher says: Your train is cancelled. Ask for a later one, and call the hostel again.
doIt.wehel: Let's practise a trip. First, you are a clerk at a train station. I book a ticket to Westhaven for Friday. Then you are a receptionist at a hostel, and I book a room. Then you are the clerk again. Tell me my train is cancelled because of a storm. Use simple English.

model.title: Booking, and a cancellation
lines: Good afternoon. Where are you travelling to?
To Westhaven, on Friday. I'd like to book a seat on the 18:05, please.
A single, please. What time does it arrive?
Harbour Hostel, good afternoon. How can I help?
Hello. I'd like to book a room for Friday night, please.
Of course. What time is your arrival?
My train gets in at 19:50, so I'll be there at about eight.
I'm sorry. Because of the storm, the 18:05 is cancelled.
Oh no. Is there a later one?
Yes, the 21:30. You can take it at no extra cost.
Hello, I've got a booking for tonight. My train's cancelled, so I'm arriving at 23:15.
No problem. Reception is open all night. See you later!
compare: Did you ask what time the train leaves or arrives?
Did you say I'd like to book… for the ticket and for the room?
When the train was cancelled, did you ask: Is there a later one?
Did you tell the hostel your new arrival time?

canDo: I can ask when a train or a coach leaves and arrives.
I can book a ticket and a room: I'd like to book…
I can choose the right future form for a trip.
I can read a timetable, a platform notice and a weather warning.
I can deal with a cancellation and write a message about a delay.

reading.before: Look at the title and the first picture. Where are the people going? What problem do you think they have?
reading.talk: Did the journey in the book go well? Tell a story about a journey with a problem, like a delay or a storm. Write two or three sentences, or say them to Wehel.

quiz.why: A timetable time: the present simple, with s.
A timetable question: When does it open?

quiz.q: My friend and I ___ in a hostel next week. We've booked it.
quiz.why: An arrangement you have booked: are + -ing.

quiz.q: At the gate, you show your passport and your ___ .
quiz.why: The boarding pass lets you get on the plane.

quiz.q: The 18:05 is cancelled. What do you ask the clerk?
quiz.why: Is there a later one? asks for a train after that time.

quiz.q: I can't see the road. There's a lot of ___ this morning.
quiz.why: Fog is thick cloud near the ground, so it is hard to see.

quiz.q: The first coach is ___ early for me. I can't get there by 5:15.
quiz.why: too + a describing word: more than you want. Too early.

quiz.q: I'm ___ the train will be late. Look at the snow!
quiz.why: I'm sure + a sentence: you are certain it is true.

quiz.q: If you press this button, the light ___ on.
quiz.why: if + present, then the present: it comes on.

liveClass: Day 1: practise the booking call in pairs. Change the trip: a coach to the airport, a train to a meeting, a ferry to an island. Ask: Is there a later one? Listen for fifteen and fifty.
Day 2: a future forms round. Show a timetable, a ticket and a to-do list. Learners say: It leaves at…, I'm flying…, I'm going to…, then decide out loud with I'll.
Day 3: the task. You are the ticket clerk and the hostel receptionist. Each learner books a ticket and a room. Then cancel their train: they ask for a later one and call the hostel again.
Day 4: talk about the book and answer questions. Read two learners' delay messages aloud: is the new time clear?
